sec: Juvenile nephronophthisis vs MCDK (ADTKD) table · p790

items.q: Match each disease with its inheritance and gene — 1) Juvenile nephronophthisis  2) MCDK1  3) MCDK2 … A) AR - NPHP1 on chromosome 2, nephrocystin  B) AD - chromosome 16, uromodulin  C) AD - chromosome 1
items.exp: JN is autosomal recessive with NPHP1 on chromosome 2 producing nephrocystin; MCDK (ADTKD) is autosomal dominant — MCDK1 on chromosome 1 and MCDK2 on chromosome 16 producing uromodulin. (Book p790)

items.q: Match each disease with its age group and ESRD timing — 1) Juvenile nephronophthisis  2) MCDK (ADTKD)  3) CTID abbreviation … A) Adults - onset by 20-25 years, ESRD by 40-50 years  B) Chronic tubulointerstitial disease  C) Children - onset by 5-7 years, ESRD by 13 years
items.exp: JN affects children, starting by 5-7 years with ESRD by 13 years; MCDK affects adults, starting by 20-25 years with ESRD by 40-50 years. The page also expands CTID as chronic tubulointerstitial disease and ADTKD as autosomal dominant tubular kidney disease. (Book p790)

items.q: In juvenile nephronophthisis, ESRD typically develops by:
items.exp: Juvenile nephronophthisis: starts by 5–7 years of age and reaches ESRD by 13 years. (Book p790)

items.q: In MCDK (ADTKD), ESRD typically develops by:
items.exp: MCDK: adults, starts by 20–25 years with ESRD by 40–50 years. (Book p790)

items.q: Match the gene defect with its product — 1) NPHP1 (chr 2)  2) MCDK₁ (chr 1)  3) MCDK₂ (chr 16) … A) Nephrocystin  B) Uromodulin  C) (Chromosome 1 locus producing its own transcript)
items.exp: Gene defects: NPHP1 on chromosome 2 → nephrocystin (defect → cilia/centrosome complex affected); MCDK₁ on chromosome 1; MCDK₂ on chromosome 16 → uromodulin. (Book p790)

items.q: Fill up: NPHP1 on chromosome 2 produces ______, whose defect affects the cilia/centrosome complex.
items.exp: NPHP1 on chr 2 → nephrocystin; defect affects the cilia/centrosome complex in juvenile nephronophthisis. (Book p790)

items.q: MCDK₂ on chromosome 16 encodes:
items.exp: MCDK₂ is on chromosome 16 and produces uromodulin (the same protein as in ADTKD). (Book p790)

items.q: Match the pathology of juvenile nephronophthisis — 1) Tubular basement membrane  2) Tubules  3) Cysts  4) Interstitium … A) Irregularity  B) Interstitial infiltration with fibrosis  C) Atrophy → CKD (CTID with shrunken kidney)  D) Few
items.exp: Pathology of juvenile nephronophthisis: tubular basement membrane irregularity; tubular atrophy → CKD (CTID with shrunken kidney); cysts few; interstitial infiltration with fibrosis. (Book p790)

items.q: In juvenile nephronophthisis the kidney becomes shrunken because of tubular atrophy, an example of chronic tubulointerstitial disease.
opts: False — the kidney becomes enlarged by multiple cysts
False — the kidney remains normal in size
items.exp: Juvenile nephronophthisis pathology: tubular atrophy → CKD, described as CTID (chronic tubulointerstitial disease) with a shrunken kidney. (Book p790)

items.q: Fill up: In juvenile nephronophthisis the cysts are ______ in number.
items.exp: Pathology of juvenile nephronophthisis: cysts are few (in contrast to the multiple cysts of ADPKD/ARPKD). (Book p790)

items.q: Match the clinical features of juvenile nephronophthisis — 1) Salt  2) Urine output  3) Growth … A) Failure to thrive  B) Polyuria  C) Wasting
items.exp: Clinical features of juvenile nephronophthisis: salt wasting, polyuria and failure to thrive. (Book p790)

items.q: Match the juvenile nephronophthisis / MCDK clinical-feature rows with their entries — 1) JN salt handling  2) JN growth  3) MCDK growth … A) Failure to thrive  B) Growth complete, so failure to thrive is absent  C) Salt wasting
items.exp: Clinical features of JN: salt wasting, polyuria and failure to thrive; MCDK is similar except for failure to thrive, because growth is complete in adults. (Book p790)

items.q: A 24-year-old adult with a strong family history of renal failure has salt wasting and polyuria but normal growth. He fits MCDK because:
opts: In MCDK the picture is similar to juvenile nephronophthisis except failure to thrive, as growth is complete
MCDK characteristically causes failure to thrive and rickets, unlike juvenile nephronophthisis
MCDK spares the tubules completely, so salt wasting and polyuria never occur
MCDK typically presents with macroscopic haematuria, renal stones and recurrent UTI
items.exp: MCDK (ADTKD) clinical features resemble JN but without failure to thrive, because growth is complete in adults. (Book p790)

items.q: Rickets-like changes are present in juvenile nephronophthisis but absent in MCDK.
opts: True — rickets-like changes from phosphorus and calcium loss are present in JN, absent in MCDK
False — rickets-like changes occur only in MCDK, where growth is complete
False — rickets-like changes are equally present in JN and in MCDK
True, but only after renal transplantation in either of the two diseases
items.exp: Rickets-like changes: present (+) in juvenile nephronophthisis due to loss of phosphorus and calcium; absent (–) in MCDK because growth is complete. (Book p790)

items.q: Match the extrarenal association with its syndrome — 1) Retinitis pigmentosa  2) Oculomotor apraxia  3) Cerebellar aplasia  4) Situs inversus … A) Cogan syndrome  B) Senior Loken syndrome  C) Joubert syndrome  D) A listed association of juvenile nephronophthisis
items.exp: Extrarenal associations of juvenile nephronophthisis: retinitis pigmentosa — Senior Loken syndrome; oculomotor apraxia — Cogan syndrome; cerebellar aplasia — Joubert syndrome; and situs inversus. (Book p790)

items.q: A 7-year-old with polyuria and growth failure also has night blindness and pigmentary retinopathy. Which eponymous syndrome is this?
items.exp: Retinitis pigmentosa with juvenile nephronophthisis = Senior Loken syndrome. (Book p790)

items.q: A child with nephronophthisis shows abnormal eye movements with difficulty initiating saccades. The named syndrome is:
items.exp: Oculomotor apraxia with juvenile nephronophthisis = Cogan syndrome. (Book p790)

items.q: Match each MCDK extrarenal association with its note — 1) Hyperuricemia and gout  2) Insulin resistance  3) Rickets-like changes in MCDK … A) Seen in the MCDK2 defect  B) Absent, because growth is complete  C) Also listed for MCDK
items.exp: MCDK extrarenal associations: hyperuricemia and gout (in the MCDK2 defect) and insulin resistance; rickets-like changes are present in JN but absent in MCDK because growth is complete. (Book p790)

items.q: Recurrence after transplant is absent in both juvenile nephronophthisis and MCDK.
opts: False — both recur in 50% of grafts
False — JN recurs but MCDK does not
items.exp: Recurrence after transplant row: absent for juvenile nephronophthisis and absent for MCDK. (Book p790)

items.q: Fill up: In the table, MCDK is abbreviated as AKA ______.
items.exp: The table heading reads 'MCDK (AKA ADTKD)' — autosomal dominant tubular kidney disease. The footnotes define CTID as chronic tubulointerstitial disease and ADTKD as autosomal dominant tubular kidney disease. (Book p790)

items.q: All but one of the following are extrarenal associations of juvenile nephronophthisis. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Insulin resistance is listed with hyperuricemia/gout as an MCDK association; the JN list contains retinitis pigmentosa, oculomotor apraxia, cerebellar aplasia (Joubert) and situs inversus. (Book p790)
